easy.def: Very happy because of a win.
examples: The jubilant fans cheered.
She was jubilant.
The team was jubilant.

more.def: Feeling and showing great joy, especially after success.
examples: The jubilant fans cheered when their team won.
She was jubilant after finishing the race.
The jubilant children danced in the rain.

easy.def: A special celebration of an anniversary.
examples: The town held a jubilee.
The jubilee was fun.
We went to the jubilee.

more.def: A special celebration of a long-lasting event, such as an anniversary.
examples: The queen celebrated her golden jubilee.
The town held a jubilee for its two hundredth birthday.
We danced at the jubilee.

easy.def: To decide who or what is best.
examples: My teacher will judge the art show.
Do not judge a book by its cover.
Who will judge the pie contest?

more.def: To form an opinion about something, or to decide the winner of a contest.
examples: Three chefs judged the baking contest.
It is hard to judge how far away the mountain is.
You should not judge people by their clothes.

easy.def: A decision about something.
examples: The judge gave her judgment.
I trust his judgment.
Use good judgment.

more.def: An opinion or decision that you make after thinking.
examples: The judge gave his judgment on the case.
I trust her good judgment.
Use good judgment when you cross the street.

easy.def: Quick to say that others are wrong.
examples: Do not be judgmental.
A judgmental look.
He was judgmental.

more.def: Quick to criticize others or to form a harsh opinion of them.
examples: Try not to be judgmental; everyone makes mistakes.
She gave a judgmental look at his messy shoes.
A good friend is kind, not judgmental.

easy.def: Showing good sense.
examples: A judicious choice.
The judicious teacher.
She was judicious.

more.def: Showing good sense and sound judgment.
examples: She made a judicious choice.
The judicious teacher solved the argument.
It was judicious to bring a coat.

easy.def: A sport where two people try to throw each other.
examples: He does judo.
Judo is a sport.
She wears a white suit for judo.

more.def: A sport in which two people try to throw each other to the ground, using balance and skill.
examples: She takes judo lessons.
Judo teaches balance and respect.
He wore a white uniform for judo.

easy.def: A large container with a handle for holding liquids.
examples: A jug of milk is in the fridge.
The jug is full.
He carried the jug.

more.def: A large container with a narrow top and a handle, used for holding liquids such as milk or juice.
examples: A jug of milk sat on the kitchen table.
He carried a water jug to the garden.
We filled the jug with fresh lemonade for the picnic.

related.def: As much as a jug holds.

easy.def: To keep objects in the air by throwing and catching them.
examples: The clown juggles balls.
I can juggle three balls.
She juggled oranges.

more.def: To keep several objects in the air at one time by tossing and catching them.
examples: The clown juggled five balls.
I can juggle three oranges.
She juggled homework and sports all week.

easy.def: A person who keeps many things in the air.
examples: The juggler tossed balls.
A juggler is at the fair.
The juggler is good.

more.def: A performer who tosses and catches several things at once.
examples: The juggler tossed five balls in the air.
A juggler performed at the fair.
The juggler caught flaming sticks.

easy.def: The wet part of fruit that you can drink.
examples: I drink orange juice.
The juice is cold.
Apple juice is sweet.

more.def: The liquid that comes out of fruits or vegetables when you squeeze them.
examples: Fresh juice dripped down his chin as he bit the peach.
We squeezed lemons to make juice for lemonade.
Carrot juice is bright orange.

related.def: A tool that squeezes juice out of fruit.

easy.def: Full of juice.
examples: The orange is sweet and juicy.
We ate juicy watermelon.
The pear is ripe and juicy.

more.def: Having a lot of juice.
examples: He bit into a ripe, juicy peach.
The grill made the chicken tender and juicy.
Bees buzzed around the juicy plums on the ground.

easy.def: A music machine that plays songs when you put in coins.
examples: We played a song on the jukebox.
The jukebox is old.
The jukebox glowed.

more.def: A machine, often found in a restaurant, that plays the song that you choose when you put in a coin.
examples: We chose three songs from the jukebox at the diner.
The old jukebox glowed with colored lights.
Grandpa dropped a coin into the jukebox and picked his favorite song.

easy.def: The month after June.
examples: We have a picnic in July.
It is hot in July.
Fireworks lit the sky in July.

more.def: The seventh month of the year, which is often the hottest in the north.
examples: Many places in the north have their hottest weather in July.
Our town has a parade on the Fourth of July.
The tomatoes in the garden are ripe by July.

easy.def: A messy mix of things.
examples: A jumble of toys was on the floor.
The jumble of letters.
A jumble of clothes lay there.

more.def: A messy mixture of things all mixed together.
examples: A jumble of toys lay on the floor.
The word puzzle was a jumble of letters.
I found my keys in a jumble of coins.

easy.def: To mix things up in a messy way.
examples: Do not jumble the cards.
The wind jumbled the papers.
He jumbled the letters.

more.def: To mix things together in a confused, messy way.
examples: The wind jumbled the papers on the desk.
He jumbled the puzzle pieces on the table.
The kitten jumbled the yarn into a knot.

easy.def: Much bigger than usual.
examples: I ate a jumbo pretzel.
The jumbo jet landed.
We bought a jumbo bag of popcorn.

more.def: Very large, much bigger than the usual size.
examples: We shared a jumbo bag of popcorn at the movie.
A jumbo jet carried hundreds of passengers across the ocean.
The jumbo pretzel was as big as my face.

easy.def: To push yourself up into the air.
examples: Frogs jump.
I jump rope.
He jumped over the puddle.

more.def: To push yourself off the ground with your legs.
examples: The cat jumped onto the windowsill.
Kangaroos can jump over fences.
She jumped across the stream.

easy.def: A push up off the ground.
examples: That was a big jump.
She made a long jump.
Her jump cleared the bar.

more.def: A leap into or through the air.
examples: The cat's jump took it onto the fence.
He won first prize in the long jump.
Her jump cleared the rope.

easy.def: A person or animal that jumps.
examples: The frog is a good jumper.
She is a high jumper.
A jumper leaped over the bar.

more.def: A person or animal that jumps, especially in a sport.
examples: The frog is the best jumper in the pond.
The high jumper cleared the bar with a graceful leap.
A good jumper bends her knees before she leaps.

easy.def: A sleeveless dress worn over a shirt.
examples: She wore a blue jumper.
My jumper has big pockets.
The jumper goes over a shirt.

more.def: A dress with no sleeves that is worn over a shirt or sweater.
examples: She wore a gray jumper over a white shirt to school.
The jumper had two deep pockets in the front.
In cold weather, I put a sweater under my jumper.

easy.def: One piece of clothing with both pants and a top.
examples: She wore a jumpsuit.
The jumpsuit is blue.
I put on a jumpsuit.

more.def: A one-piece piece of clothing that covers the body, arms and legs.
examples: The mechanic wore a blue jumpsuit.
She zipped up her red jumpsuit.
The astronaut's jumpsuit was bright orange.

easy.def: Easily scared or nervous.
examples: The cat is jumpy.
I feel jumpy at night.
He was jumpy before the show.

more.def: Nervous or easily startled, so you jump at small sounds or surprises.
examples: After the loud thunder, the puppy was jumpy for the rest of the night.
She felt jumpy before the big spelling bee.
The jumpy horse shied at every shadow on the trail.

easy.def: A place where roads or tracks meet.
examples: We stopped at the junction.
The roads meet at a junction.
The train stopped at the junction.

more.def: A place where two or more roads, tracks or paths join.
examples: The bus turned left at the junction.
Several train lines meet at a busy junction.
A sign at the junction pointed to the lake.

easy.def: The sixth month of the year.
examples: School ends in June.
Summer starts in June.
We swim in the lake in June.

more.def: The sixth month of the year, when summer begins in many places.
examples: The longest day of the year is in June.
Fireflies begin to glow in the evenings in June.
My cousins visit us every June.

easy.def: A hot place with lots of trees and plants.
examples: Monkeys live in the jungle.
A snake hides in the jungle.
The jungle is wet and green.

more.def: A thick forest in a hot, rainy part of the world.
examples: Bright parrots flew through the jungle.
Explorers cut a path through the thick jungle.
The jungle was noisy with the calls of birds and frogs.

easy.def: Younger or lower in rank.
examples: He is a junior member.
A junior high school.
The junior class.

more.def: Younger, or lower in rank.
examples: He is a junior member of the team.
My brother is in the junior class.
She is a junior reporter.

easy.def: A small green bush with blue fruit.
examples: A juniper grew on the hill.
The juniper stays green.
Birds eat juniper berries.

more.def: An evergreen bush or small tree with needle-like leaves and small blue berries.
examples: A juniper grew near the rocky edge of the cliff.
Birds feed on juniper berries in winter.
Junipers stay green all year, even in snow.

easy.def: Old things that are no longer useful.
examples: The garage is full of junk.
We threw out the junk.
The box is full of junk.

more.def: Old things that nobody wants or needs.
examples: The garage is full of old junk.
We took the junk to the dump.
He found a few treasures in the pile of junk.

easy.def: A place where old, broken things are kept.
examples: The old car is in the junkyard.
We went to the junkyard.
The junkyard is full of metal.

more.def: An outdoor place where old cars, machines and other things that people no longer want are collected.
examples: The old truck ended up in the junkyard with rows of other broken cars.
Dad found a part for our bicycle at the junkyard.
The junkyard was full of rusty metal and old tires.

easy.def: The biggest planet in our solar system.
examples: Jupiter is a giant planet.
Jupiter is the biggest planet.
Jupiter is far from the sun.

more.def: The largest planet in our solar system, fifth from the sun.
examples: Jupiter is the biggest planet.
Jupiter has a giant red spot.
Jupiter has dozens of moons.

easy.def: From the time of dinosaurs long ago.
examples: The Jurassic period.
Jurassic dinosaurs were big.
It is a Jurassic fossil.

more.def: Describing the time about 150 million years ago when many large dinosaurs lived.
examples: Many dinosaurs lived in the Jurassic period.
We saw a Jurassic fossil at the museum.
The Jurassic age had giant plant eaters.

easy.def: A person on a jury.
examples: The juror listened.
A juror was chosen.
The jurors voted.

more.def: A person who is chosen to listen to a trial and help decide the result.
examples: The juror listened to the case.
Twelve jurors were chosen.
The jurors voted together.

easy.def: A group of people who decide a case in court.
examples: The jury listened to the story.
The jury made a choice.
A jury sits in a court.

more.def: A group of people in a court who listen to a case and decide what is true.
examples: The jury listened to both sides of the story.
Twelve people sat on the jury.
The jury decided the man was not guilty.

easy.def: Only, or a very short time ago.
examples: I want just one cookie.
We just got home.
It is just a little bug.

more.def: Only or simply, or a very short time before now.
examples: There is just enough paint left to finish the fence.
The bell just rang, so the class is over.
I am just going to rest for a minute.

easy.def: Being fair to everyone.
examples: Justice means the rules are fair for all.
The judge wants justice.
Heroes in stories fight for justice.

more.def: Fair treatment for everyone, following what is right.
examples: The judge worked hard to make sure there was justice.
The people marched to ask for justice.
A fair trial is an important part of justice.

easy.def: Having a good reason.
examples: His anger was justifiable.
A justifiable choice.
It is justifiable.

more.def: Having a good reason so that it can be accepted.
examples: His worry was justifiable.
A justifiable choice made sense.
It was justifiable to stay home in the storm.

easy.def: A good reason for doing something.
examples: He gave a justification.
There was no justification.
What is your justification?

more.def: A good reason or explanation for something that someone did.
examples: He gave no justification for being late.
The teacher asked for a justification for the answer.
There is no justification for being unkind.

easy.def: To give a good reason for something.
examples: I cannot justify what I did.
She justified her choice.
He justified his answer.

more.def: To show that something is right or fair by giving good reasons.
examples: I cannot justify taking the last cookie without asking.
She justified her answer with facts.
The scientist justified the test with a clear reason.

easy.def: In a fair way.
examples: He was justly rewarded.
She acted justly.
The prize was justly won.

more.def: In a fair and right way.
examples: The winner was justly rewarded.
The judge acted justly.
She was justly proud.

easy.def: To stick out.
examples: A rock juts out.
The branch jutted from the wall.
The dock juts into the lake.

more.def: To stick out farther than the things around it.
examples: A rocky point juts out into the sea.
The balcony juts out over the garden.
A shelf jutted from the wall and I bumped my head.

easy.def: A plant fiber used to make rope and sacks.
examples: Jute makes rope.
The sack is jute.
Jute is strong.

more.def: A strong fiber from a plant, used to make rope and sacks.
examples: The sack was made of jute.
Jute is used to make rope.
The rug was woven from jute.

easy.def: Young, or like a child.
examples: A juvenile bird.
The juvenile eagle.
Juvenile fish.

more.def: Young, or having to do with young people; also, silly and childish.
examples: The juvenile eagle has darker feathers than an adult.
Juvenile fish swim in the shallow water.
The shop sold juvenile books.
